title: Policy-driven load probe and scheduler feedback protocol
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary
-------
This page documents the Policy-driven Load Probe and Scheduler Feedback Protocol (PLP-SFP). The protocol is designed to safely surface scheduler and kernel behavior under controlled, policy-shaped load while providing deterministic feedback signals that the runtime scheduler can consume to adjust admission, backfill, and priority heuristics.

Intended audience
- Runtime engineers
- Benchmarking and perf-sig members
- Oncall and SRE rotation responsible for scheduler incidents

Goals
- Provide a reproducible method for injecting targeted load shapes into the serving runtime without violating customer SLAs.
- Produce canonical telemetry artifacts (probe reports) that map directly to scheduler decision signals.
- Define automated feedback actions the scheduler can take when probes indicate a regression or resource pressure.

Scope and non-goals
- In scope: admission/backfill behavior, KV cache warmup under shaped bursts, per-kernel latency distribution under mixed-concurrency, slot coalescing effectiveness.
- Out of scope: long-running model training, hardware-level failure injections (handled by infra chaos team).

Glossary
- Probe: controlled synthetic traffic pattern exercised against a target model and route.
- Fingerprint: compact summary of latency/cost distribution for a probe (see Probe fingerprint format).
- Decision signal: normalized metric emitted by the probe runner that the scheduler consumes (e.g., kernel contention score, slot-utilization drift).

Architecture overview
1) Controller: probe-runner service (bench-probe) that schedules probes and collects traces. Owned by benchmarking team.
2) Collector: high-throughput telemetry pipeline that annotates traces with request-provenance and kernel hints. Uses the runtime trace bus.
3) Aggregator: offline/nearline job that produces a probe fingerprint and decision signals. Runs in namespace perf-aggregator.
4) Consumer: scheduler decision fabric subscribes to decision signals via the signal bus and maps signals to policy actions (admit/reject/backfill/tier-shift).

Probe types and recommended usage
- Smoke probe: short (30s) steady QPS at nominal concurrency. Use for CI verifications.
- Burst probe: 5–60s high-intensity spike aimed at stressing KV cache and kernel preemption. Use for degradation mode tests.
- Ramp probe: linear ramp from 10% to 110% nominal QPS over 5–10 minutes to find nonlinear breakpoints.
- Cohort probe: multi-route correlated traffic that exercises cross-tenant memory eviction and kernel-sharing.

Probe configuration (recommended defaults)
| field                  | description                                              | default        | notes |
|------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|----------------|-------|
| model                  | model variant to exercise (e.g., gptx-3-8b-quant)        | required       | pick a representative variant |
| duration_seconds       | probe wall time                                           | 60             | adjust for probe type |
| qps_target             | aggregate queries per second                              | 50             | expressed at client ingress |
| concurrency_target     | target in-flight requests                                 | 8              | prefer 1–32 |
| input_seq_length       | input token length distribution (CSV of percentiles)      | 8,32,128       | used to exercise kernel breakpoints |
| trace_level            | trace/detail (none|header|full)                           | header         | full increases telemetry cost |
| allow_fallbacks        | whether probe may trigger model fallback                  | false          | keep false for fidelity baseline |

Probe fingerprint format
- single-line canonicalization: <probe-name> | <median-lat-ms> | <p95-lat-ms> | <cost-per-token-µs> | <kv-hit-rate> | <kernel-contention-score>
- store fingerprints in perf-store keyed by probe id and commit sha.

Operational procedure: running a scheduled probe
1) Author probe manifest and check against policy validator: bench-probe validate <manifest.yaml>.
2) Schedule in bench-probe: bench-probe run --manifest manifest.yaml --dry-run (dry-run verifies signal wiring without emitting traffic).
3) Execute during a controlled window (must coordinate with SRE). Add marker to rollout calendar.
4) After run, wait for aggregator job to publish the fingerprint artifact.
5) Review report in perf-dashboard and file any anomalies in the perf-issue tracker with tag "plp-sfp".

Example probe manifest (manifest.yaml)
---
probe_name: "kv-warmup-burst-az1"
model: "redwood/gptx-3-8b-quant-v2"
duration_seconds: 45
qps_target: 250
concurrency_target: 12
input_seq_length: "8,32,128"
trace_level: "header"
allow_fallbacks: false
---

Telemetry and key metrics to collect
- request_latency_ms (p50/p90/p95/p99) broken out by kernel and end-to-end
- kernel_queue_depth and kernel_dispatch_time_ms
- kv_cache_hit_rate and kv_locality_ratio
- token_throughput and token_cost_estimate_us
- kernel_contention_score: synthetic metric combining kernel-wait time and preemption counts

Automated feedback and mapping to scheduler actions
- If kernel_contention_score > 0.45 for sustained 30s: reduce admit rate for affected slot by 30% and enable slot-coalescing for that cohort for 2 minutes.
- If kv_cache_hit_rate falls below 0.6 during burst probe: prioritize pre-warmed slots (warmstart=true) and temporarily prefer slot affinity to nodes with warm caches.
- If p99 request_latency exceeds configured SLO + 2x baseline during a smoke probe: mark the latest deployment as suspect and open a canary rollback action.

Policy validation rules (validator checks)
- Probes must not target production tenant routes unless a written SLA waiver exists.
- qps_target * duration_seconds must be within the probe window budget assigned to the bench namespace.
- allow_fallbacks must be false for fidelity-critical probes.

Scheduler mapping examples
- Decision signal: {kernel_contention: 0.52, cohort: "search-heavy"} -> Action: cohort_priority -= 1; trigger_backfill_threshold=0.65; run eviction-smoothing for 90s.
- Decision signal: {kv_hit: 0.45, node_affinity: [n1,n2]} -> Action: nominate pull-warmslot job for nodes n1,n2; increase preferred_affinity_weight for 60s.

Runbook: probe-caused outage mitigation (oncall steps)
1) Identify active probes via bench-probe events and correlate with perf ingest times.
2) If production SLOs are impacted: disable probe by ID immediately (bench-probe cancel <id>).
3) Escalate to scheduler-owner and runtime-oncall. Attach probe fingerprint to the incident ticket.
4) If degradation persists after probe cancellation, run the rollback matrix: a) reduce admission to reserve 20% capacity for critical routes b) enable coarse-grained fallback routes for enterprise customers.
5) Post-incident: run a shaded replay of the probe in a canary namespace and collect aggregated artifacts for root cause analysis.

Reporting and dashboards
- perf-dashboard/plp-sfp: single-pane view showing live probe status, fingerprint changes over time, vulnerable cohorts, and aggregated decision signals.
- Alerting: probe-failure (job failed to complete), probe-sla-impact (if probe correlates to any route SLO breach within 1m), probe-signal-spike (kernel_contention > 0.5).

Automation and CI integration
- Short smoke probes run on every runtime scheduler merge to main. CI job: bench-probe ci-run --manifest ci-smoke.yaml.
- Longer ramp and burst probes are gated behind an internal release window and require SRE approval.

Ownership and contacts
- Primary owner: Benchmarking team (owner group: eng-serving-runtime-benchmarking).
- Scheduler consumer: Runtime Scheduler team (contact: @arjun.patel).
- Oncall escalation: runtime-oncall rotation.

Related artifacts and references
- Probe runner implementation: git://repo/bench-probe (internal)
- Fingerprint schema: perf-store/docs/fingerprint-spec.md
- Scheduler signal bus contract: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/scheduler-telemetry-synthesis-and-proofing-2025.json

Change log
- 2026-01-12: Draft created by Maya Chen.
- 2026-03-02: Added probe fingerprint schema and initial mapping rules.
- 2026-09-04: Updated automated feedback thresholds and example manifest; added runbook steps for probe-caused outages.

Appendix: troubleshooting checklist
- If aggregator fails to produce fingerprint: verify telemetry pipeline health, ensure bench-probe wrote trace ids to perf-ingest, check S3 bucket for raw traces.
- If scheduler ignored decision signals: confirm signal bus ACLs, confirm consumer subscription, validate schema version alignment.
- If KV warmup did not occur: check warmstart job logs and node affinity assignments.
